newsitem.title: FINLAND: PROTOS SAYS FINNISH INTEREST RATES HAVE BOTTOMED.
newsitem.headline: PROTOS SAYS FINNISH INTEREST RATES HAVE BOTTOMED.

text.p: Brokerage Davy Protos Stockbrokers said on Thursday that Finnish interest rates have bottomed and that it is expecting a moderate rise in rates in Finland as well as in Europe.

"We have seen the bottom of the current interest rate cycle, now we expect a moderate rise in interest rates in Finland as well as in Europe," Protos managing director Ari Lahti told a news conference.
In a report, Protos said the 10-year Finnish/German bond yield gap would be between 50 and 75 basis points in 1997.
"The (10-year) yield premium over Germany will not narrow significantly from current levels (around 60 bps) because there is uncertainty whether EMU will come about," Lahti said.
Protos said the 10-year benchmark 2006 bond yield will rise 20 basis points by March next year, and by a total of some 50 basis points to around 6.90 percent by summer.
It repeated an earlier forecast that it expects a hike in the Bank of Finland's key tender rate in the near term.
"The Bank of Finland should take care that its credibility as the guardian of inflation does not suffer," Lahti said.
"This way, a more stable growth path would be established in the longer term," he said.
The central bank's chief monetary policy tool, the tender rate, has been unchanged at 3.00 percent since October 9 when it was cut from 3.10 percent.
